change: Standalone midpoint workers use a concrete WindowRangeMidpoint.State kernel instead of the generic IIndicatorState wrapper. FrameworkCompatibility.IsFinite uses the modern runtime intrinsic with an inline hint; NETFRAMEWORK retains its existing portable predicate. Arithmetic, storage, scheduling, mixed-batch behavior and public API are unchanged.
profile: dotnet-trace 10.0.750501 on Windows collected dotnet-sampled-thread-time against the existing 10k close-midpoint BuilderFull binary. This is sampled managed thread time, not kernel CPU-cycle sampling. before.speedscope.json.gz retains the capture. profile-summary includes only intervals with ComputeBoundedRegion on the stack, attributes leaves after removing synthetic CPU_TIME/UNMANAGED_CODE_TIME markers, and also reports the last active second. Worker scope totals 6107.46 ms across 3368 intervals; interface thunk attribution is 14.18% overall / 10.92% in the last active second, and portable finite-check attribution is 6.00% / 5.20%. Percentages are not predicted end-to-end speedups.
capture_limitation: After workload execution, BenchmarkDotNet report export stalled reading a child dotnet --version process that inherited diagnostic startup suspension. The child was independently identified by parent PID and exact command line and stopped after resume did not release it. The benchmark process was not restarted and the original capture completed. Reporting/idle waits are excluded by worker-stack scope. No latency measured under the profiler is selected as benchmark evidence.
measurements: Eight new builder cases use five warmups and fifteen measured iterations without a profiler. Qualification retains the fastest native arms and earlier 100k rows with checked source provenance; 100k was not remeasured in this batch. Close-midpoint 1k LatestOnly improves from 14.12 to 12.80 us, but Full latency remains essentially unchanged. Final 10k Full close/high-low times are 107.93/102.69 us and LatestOnly is 69.66/71.45 us. Both operations still lose to native parallel; no closed gap or broad latency win is claimed.
remaining: Worker-local dispatch reduction alone does not eliminate the end-to-end cost difference. Snapshot/publication and scheduling costs remain candidates for targeted investigation. Direct qualification remains 91 APIs and the full rollout is incomplete.
